# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile details beyond the existence of three cuttable wire positions, and I have received no instructions or observations. I need the manual’s rule and Deaf’s visual description before acting. I will ask Mute to relay the required procedure and establish any needed gesture encoding for Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3. I have no other tactile details. Please tell me the manual rule and relay any needed visual questions or gesture code.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, white light, and wires: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Do not act yet; I am obtaining Mute's manual instruction.

Deaf has identified the bomb as display 0 with a white light and wires ordered yellow, green, blue, but explicitly says not to act while Mute’s instruction is being obtained. I should not cut anything yet. I will ask Mute directly for the applicable manual rule, including the required wire position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Please give the exact manual instruction and cut position when determined; I will not act until then.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visible state: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute sent the gesture ?, but its meaning is not established. Do not operate anything yet.
Deaf says to Blind: If Mute sends a clear numbered gesture sequence, I will repeat its symbol names and the visible state.

Mute can hear me but cannot speak, while Deaf can see Mute’s gestures and can speak their description to me. I will establish a simple unambiguous relay: Mute should gesture 👍 repeated once, twice, or three times to mean cut wire 1, 2, or 3. Deaf can then count the repeated symbols and tell me the result aloud. No action is safe until that relay is complete.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual's required cut: gesture thumbs-up 👍 once means wire 1, twice means wire 2, three times means wire 3. Send only that many thumbs-up gestures. Deaf, please relay the count aloud to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state now: display 0, red light; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute signalled a three-part sequence that appears to mean 2, 3, 1. If this is the manual action order, operate wires in order: wire 2 green, then wire 3 blue, then wire 1 yellow.

Deaf’s report does not confirm that the three-part gesture is an established instruction; it may be an unagreed encoding rather than the manual’s required action order. Cutting a wire before confirmation is unsafe. I need Mute to use the explicit repeated-thumbs-up code I just defined, and Deaf to relay its count exactly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send an unlabelled sequence. Using our code, send 👍 once for cut wire 1, 👍👍 for wire 2, or 👍👍👍 for wire 3. If the manual requires multiple cuts in order, send each instruction separated by a clear pause and have Deaf state the symbol sequence.")
speak(to="deaf", text="Please do not infer an action from the earlier 2,3,1 sequence. Tell me the exact gesture symbols Mute makes after receiving the thumbs-up code, including grouping or order.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state now: display 0; light white; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's newest exact gesture sequence is: OK-hand, then raised open back-of-hand (? ?). I cannot safely map that to a wire; do not act unless it matches a manual instruction you can identify by touch.

My previous messages were not delivered, because I attempted to use speech toward Deaf, who cannot hear. The only reliable spoken channel from me is to Mute. I will send Mute one clear instruction: encode the manual’s selected wire using repetitions of the literal thumbs-up gesture. Deaf can observe and report that count verbally to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please use this agreed code now: make literal thumbs-up gesture 👍 once if the manual says cut wire 1, twice if wire 2, three times if wire 3. Do not use other gestures. Deaf will tell me the count.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visible state: display 0; purple light; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's newest exact signal is thumbs up, ?. Its physical meaning is not yet unambiguous; do not act yet.

Mute’s latest response still contains an extra, unidentified gesture, so it cannot safely be read as the repetition-count code. I will restate the code with an explicit failure response and wait for a gesture string containing only the agreed symbol.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your last reply included an unknown extra gesture, so I cannot act. Reply with ONLY these symbols and no separator: 👍 = cut wire 1; 👍👍 = cut wire 2; 👍👍👍 = cut wire 3. If you cannot give one of those exact replies, send only 👎. Deaf will relay exactly what you send.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visible state: display 0; red light; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute has again signalled thumbs up. This is the same gesture Mute sent when the light was purple; no physical action has been established from it.

Mute received my explicit code and has now replied with exactly one thumbs-up gesture. Under that code, one 👍 means the manual selects wire position 1. Deaf could not independently interpret the code because Deaf cannot hear my spoken agreement with Mute, but I can. I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
